newsitem.title: UK: Grandmet slams LVMH demerger plans.
newsitem.headline: Grandmet slams LVMH demerger plans.

text.p: British drinks and food giant Grand Metropolitan plc on Friday slammed a demerger proposal by French LVMH Moet Hennessy Louis Vuitton SA and said it would result in a value loss of 1.5 billion pounds ($2.5 billion) and possibly "significantly more".
Grand Met said its planned 24 billion pound merger with Guinness Plc was "on track" and the timetable unaffected by the LVMH objections.

The GrandMet statement came one day after LVMH Chairman Bernard Arnault flew back to Paris after meeting with three to four major shareholders in Guinness and Grand Metropolitan to reiterate his plans for a three-way merger of the firms.

The French luxury goods to spirits company also said in a statement released in London that its plans for such a merger would lead to further cost savings of 65 million pounds ($108.9 million) over and above what the British companies identified in their own two-way merger plan.

But GrandMet and Guinness said on Friday their boards have "unanimously concluded that the LVMH demerger proposal would result in a substantial loss of shareholder value for the GMG Brands (the Guinness-GrandMet merger) shareholders other than LVMH".

"Under LVMH's proposals, our other shareholders would end up significantly worse off than under the GMG Brands proposal. An immediate demerger would destroy rather than create value and we cannot countenance LVMH taking value from our other shareholders in the manner proposed," the Guinness and GrandMet chairmen said in a joint statement.
GrandMet's George Bull and Guinness chairman Tony Greener said the completion of the GMG Brands merger is targeted for January, subject to regulatory and shareholder approval.
But they said they would still consider future LVMH proposals that "adds to the value created by GMG Brands and which provides for a fair sharing of such incremental value."
They said the LVMH proposal was "fundamentally inequitable" and that LVMH's 66 percent share in drinks company Moet Hennessy was "not important" to the GMG merger.
